item.title: Explainer: Two deadly crashes in nine months: What's happening to Spain's high-speed rail?
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
MADRID, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- Just nine months after a deadly railway accident near Adamuz in southern Spain, another high-speed train collision occurred on Wednesday on the same Madrid-Seville railway line, raising renewed concerns about the safety of Spain's high-speed rail network. The collision between two high-speed trains near Urda station in Toledo province, central Spain, has killed at least 68 people and injured 180 more. WHAT HAPPENED AND WHY? At around 8:54 a.m. local time (0754 GMT) on Wednesday, a Renfe-operated AVE train carrying 378 passengers struck the rear of a stationary Iryo train with 147 passengers aboard near Urda station. Both trains were heading from Madrid to Seville, according to Spain's Ministry of Transport and railway operator Renfe. At least 68 were killed, according to the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha. More than 180 people were reported injured, with some in critical condition. Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente said at a press conference on Wednesday afternoon that the LZB train safety system had failed at around 8:30 a.m. due to a communication problem involving three computers, affecting a 63-km section of the railway and automatically bringing several trains to a halt. According to Puente, Adif's control center subsequently authorized the AVE train to resume normal operations at around 8:36 a.m., despite a red signal and the presence of the stationary Iryo train ahead. The AVE traveled approximately 25 km before crashing into the Iryo at around 8:53 a.m.. Under Spanish railway safety regulations, trains must remain stopped when the LZB system fails and the track ahead is occupied. Any authorized movement must follow restricted operating procedures requiring drivers to maintain a speed that allows them to stop upon detecting an obstacle ahead. Puente described the control center's decision as "inexplicable," while railway engineering expert Ramiro Aurin told Spanish news agency EFE that human error was the most likely explanation for the collision. However, the exact circumstances and responsibilities remain under investigation. GOVERNMENT RESPONSE AND PUBLIC SCRUTINY The tragedy prompted the Spanish government and several major political parties to suspend their scheduled activities on Wednesday. During a visit to the accident site in Urda, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez stressed that rescuing victims and supporting their families remained the government's top priority. He pledged a thorough investigation into the collision, saying that any negligence or failures in railway safety systems would be addressed. "We will get to the bottom of this," Sanchez said. The government also declared three days of national mourning from Oct. 29 to Oct. 31, while the regional government of Castilla-La Mancha activated an emergency response plan and mobilized additional rescue and medical resources. Several hospitals suspended scheduled activities to accommodate the injured, while psychological support teams were deployed to assist victims and their families. The accident also triggered calls for accountability. Opposition People's Party (PP) leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo said Spain had the right to know what was happening with its railway infrastructure. He called for immediate government and judicial investigations, as well as a comprehensive and independent review of the country's entire railway network. In Madrid, hundreds of demonstrators gathered outside the Ministry of Transport on Wednesday evening, demanding the resignation of the Transport Minister Puente. Railway unions also called for stronger safety safeguards. The Independent Trade Union and Civil Servants' Central (CSIF) demanded an urgent explanation of the accident, accountability for those responsible, and greater investment in railway infrastructure and maintenance. The Spanish train drivers' union Semaf said it would proceed with a strike scheduled for Thursday, calling for stronger railway safety guarantees and structural reforms. The union also said it was considering further action following the latest tragedy. GROWING CONCERNS OVER RAIL SAFETY The collision marks Spain's second major fatal high-speed rail accident this year, with a crash near Adamuz, in the southern province of Cordoba, claiming 46 lives on Jan. 18. While investigations into both accidents remain ongoing, experts have pointed to different possible causes. Jordi Vinolas Prat, a mechanical engineering professor at Francisco de Vitoria University, told Europa Press that the Adamuz disaster appeared to be linked to railway infrastructure problems, while the latest collision raised questions about signaling systems. Jose Trigueros, president of the Association of Civil Engineers, told Spanish national broadcaster RTVE that the latest collision was particularly concerning because high-speed rail safety systems were designed to prevent two trains from occupying the same section of track. He questioned the reliability of automated safety protections and the extent to which railway operations depended on human intervention. Concerns over railway safety had already been raised following the Adamuz disaster. Rafael Escudero, secretary-general of the Sindicato Ferroviario railway union, told Spanish radio station Onda Cero that the union had called for an audit of renovation works on the Madrid-Seville high-speed line after the January accident. He urged a review of how the more than 700 million euros (770 million U.S. dollars) allocated to upgrading the line had been spent, while stressing that the cause of Wednesday's collision remained under investigation. The latest tragedy has also unsettled some railway passengers. Daniel, a frequent traveler between Malaga and Madrid, told Spanish radio station Cadena SER that the accident had left him feeling angry and insecure, saying recent railway incidents had undermined his confidence in train travel. Civil engineer Martin Perea, a transport specialist and master's program director at Universidad Europea, also warned of serious damage to the reputation of Spain's railway system, calling for a thorough investigation, support for victims and their families, and a broader reassessment of the country's high-speed rail operations. ■

item.title: China's farm machinery industry moves upmarket, reaches abroad
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
TIANJIN, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- Some of the farm machinery produced at German manufacturer CLAAS's factory in east China's Shandong Province is shipped to Europe, making the plant part of the company's global manufacturing network. The factory in Gaomi City has been operating for more than a decade, combining production with research and development and technical training. It manufactures machinery for both Chinese and overseas markets and provides manufacturing services to other CLAAS plants. "Exporting helps us improve the products we manufacture for Chinese customers," said Thomas Spiering, executive vice president of CLAAS, adding that meeting international quality standards also helps the company refine its manufacturing processes. Spiering was among the international executives attending the China International Agricultural Machinery Exhibition (CIAME) 2026, held in north China's Tianjin Municipality from Monday to Wednesday. The event brought together more than 3,000 exhibitors from China and abroad. China is a major market for farm machinery. In 2025, the country's comprehensive mechanization rate for crop plowing, sowing and harvesting reached 76.82 percent, according to the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs. U.S. manufacturer John Deere, which has operated in China for 50 years, plans to introduce new models which are designed specifically for Chinese farms and manufactured locally, targeting precision farming, autonomous operations and greener agricultural production. Tianjin has long been an important manufacturing and operational base for the company, said Sun Baolin, president of John Deere China. "We have built our presence here over the years and have grown together with many of our customers and partners," Sun added. Changes in China's manufacturing capabilities are apparent to longtime overseas buyers, and Chinese-made farm machinery and components are also reaching more overseas customers. In the first eight months of 2026, China's exports of agricultural machinery, equipment and parts rose 21.95 percent year on year to 15.11 billion U.S. dollars, the China Chamber of Commerce for Import and Export of Machinery and Electronic Products revealed. Among the Chinese manufacturers moving into more powerful agricultural equipment is Zoomlion Agriculture Machinery Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of Zoomlion Heavy Industry Science & Technology Co., Ltd., one of China's leading high-tech equipment manufacturers. At CIAME 2026, the company unveiled its 9DX hybrid tractor, designed for large-scale farming and with a peak output of 1,600 horsepower. Zoomlion said it independently developed the tractor's digital chassis, core components and control systems. The company noted that the machine was designed to improve field efficiency and reduce fuel consumption. Huo Xiaofeng, deputy general manager of Zoomlion Agriculture Machinery, said the company has also made advances in autonomous driving, adaptive tillage-depth control and other technologies, with some intelligent components already in mass production. Some of its products have reached markets including Russia, Australia and Kazakhstan. Nicolas Meunier, director of global electronic and electrical engineering at U.S. agricultural machinery manufacturer AGCO Corporation, said he was struck by the technology on display in Tianjin and the speed at which new Chinese competitors were emerging. "A few years ago, we mainly saw low-horsepower tractors from Chinese manufacturers. Today, we are seeing high-horsepower tractors, including some very large models," he said. Meunier added that the pace of development had been impressive, and that advances in technology and closer market ties could create further opportunities for cooperation between Chinese and international manufacturers. ■

item.title: African businesses eye new opportunities as China import expo approaches
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
* With China's zero-tariff treatment for 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations having taken effect on May 1, African businesses are looking to the expo to tap the Chinese market and move up the value chain through product processing, brand development and other higher-value activities. NAIROBI, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- In Kigali, Rwanda's capital, Grace Mbabazi, founder and CEO of M&M Sozo Ltd., is busy selecting the company's signature honey products ahead of her upcoming trip to China for the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), where she hopes to showcase the Rwandan specialty to a wider Chinese audience. Scheduled to take place in Shanghai from Nov. 5 to 10, this year's expo will bring together returning African exhibitors and newcomers alike. With China's zero-tariff treatment for 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations having taken effect on May 1, African businesses are looking to the expo to tap the Chinese market and move up the value chain through product processing, brand development and other higher-value activities. NEW FACES, NEW PRODUCTS This year's CIIE will welcome a number of new African friends, with Gabon making its debut at the national pavilion and Cote d'Ivoire participating collectively for the first time, injecting fresh momentum into China-Africa trade and economic cooperation. Cote d'Ivoire is seeking to further expand its presence in the Chinese market through the CIIE. Kaladji Fadiga, director of the Cote d'Ivoire Export Agency, told Xinhua that the country would focus on five key sectors at this year's expo: cocoa, coffee, cashew, kola nuts and textiles. "Our ambition is to make this edition a remarkable showcase that reflects the true potential of our trade with China," he added. Asnath Adje, head of Cote d'Ivoire's Lya Bissap brand, was delighted to learn that her company had been selected to exhibit at the CIIE. She hopes to introduce hibiscus, a plant familiar to many Ivorians since childhood, to a wider international audience in new forms. At this year's expo, she plans to showcase hibiscus powder, ultrafine powder and concentrate. The ultrafine powder can be used in food processing and cosmetics, opening up new possibilities for downstream product development, Adje said. African companies will also bring a diverse range of distinctive products to the expo. Bansa, a brand from Cameroon, plans to showcase a variety of agricultural and processed products, including roasted sesame seeds, spicy dried meat, sesame brittle made with pure honey, processed cocoa products, shea butter and plantain chips. "This is my first time participating in the CIIE as an official exhibitor. Last year, I attended as an observer," said Ngoyonga Chaswe Clotilde, a Bansa representative. Clotilde said she hopes the expo will help promote the brand to a global audience and forge partnerships that could attract investment and support further processing in Cameroon. NEW GROWTH China's market has brought tangible benefits for African businesses, with rising export volumes among the most notable. Kenya's tea exports to China rose from about 2 million kg annually in the past to 12.4 million kg in 2025, and are expected to reach around 20 million kg in 2026, said Willy Mutai, chief executive officer of the Tea Board of Kenya. Ethiopian coffee company AWO Coffee has also recorded strong growth in China. Its marketing manager, Kaleab Fekad, said the company began exporting to China in 2014, initially shipping only dozens of tonnes annually. In 2025, its exports reached 200 tonnes. AWO Coffee has expanded its offerings from raw beans to roasted beans and packaged coffee powder. After its first CIIE presence last year, the company recognized the expo's potential for brand promotion and sales, particularly for processed products. It is returning this year to reach more Chinese consumers and further expand its sales, Fekad said. The CIIE has also helped African businesses forge commercial partnerships. Wendy Mpendulo, founder of South African nut producer Miante Manufacturing, said that at last year's expo, she met a packaging company manager who expressed interest in appointing her as its representative in South Africa and using the country as a starting point to expand into other African markets. For Cameroon-based company Africa SARL, the expo has helped establish lasting trade relationships. Its chief executive officer, Pitndap Nchandini Ismaila, said he met Chinese partners at his first CIIE last year, and some of whom have since begun working with the company. "Thanks to the expo, I was able to meet Chinese partners with whom we now work closely," he said. "Our cooperation has enabled me to expand our plantations and increase exports to China." China's favorable trade policy toward Africa has provided an additional boost by lowering the cost of accessing the Chinese market. Mutai said Kenyan tea exporters could save 15 percent in tariffs by obtaining certificates of origin issued by the Kenya Revenue Authority, allowing them to benefit from China's zero-tariff arrangements. He said inquiries about Kenyan tea have increased noticeably, with Chinese buyers recently traveling to Kenya specifically to seek tea supplies. "It is a big opportunity for Kenya, and we can leverage it to sell more tea," he added. NEW MOMENTUM The zero-tariff treatment and China's vast market are also creating incentives for industrial upgrading in African countries. From understanding Chinese demand to raising local production capacity, African businesses are seeking to turn market access into long-term development opportunities. Repeated participation in the CIIE has helped Zimbabwean leather goods exporter Samuneti Leathers gain a clearer understanding of Chinese consumer preferences. "We have managed to analyze and understand our customers and what they need, and we are able to give them what they want and need," said Dionne Chibaya, an administrator at Samuneti Leathers. Building on these insights, the company plans to showcase its finest handcrafted products at this year's expo while gaining a deeper understanding of the market to guide its expansion. With a long tradition of leather craftsmanship, supported by its livestock sector and diverse wildlife resources, Zimbabwe is seeking to increase exports of value-added leather products. The CIIE offers Zimbabwean producers an opportunity to reach Chinese buyers and explore new business prospects. Madagascar's mutton made its debut at the seventh CIIE in 2024. The entry into the Chinese market has not only benefited local herders but has also energized the whole "farm-to-table" chain, creating large numbers of direct and indirect jobs, particularly for young people in rural areas. "From livestock farming and transportation to meat cutting, slaughtering and exports to China, every stage creates jobs for the Malagasy people," Madagascar's Minister of Livestock Riana Nantenaina Randrianomenjanahary said in a recent interview with Xinhua. He said at least 3,000 households benefit from this export-related activity. Madagascar is stepping up efforts to "improve local production and the value chain, while encouraging a growing number of livestock farmers to join this sector oriented toward the Chinese market," the minister said. (Video reporters: Deng Bingxue, Chen Shaohua, Fan Haoyu; Video editors: Liang Wanshan, Roger Lott, Wei Yin, Zhang Yuhong, Liu Yutian)■

item.title: Chinese design gives exports new edge at Canton Fair
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
GUANGZHOU, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- Stainless steel has long endured a rather understated existence. It can be found in kitchen sinks, saucepans and rubbish bins, having proved durable and practical but unglamorous. At the 140th China Import and Export Fair in Guangzhou in south China's Guangdong Province, however, a Chinese jewelry maker is giving this metal a different purpose. Its display of gold-toned, silver-colored and brightly hued ornaments has drawn crowds of overseas buyers at this fair, which is also known as the Canton Fair. These pieces look like fine jewelry, but most are made of stainless steel, offering a polished finish without the price tag of precious metals. For consumers, the proposition is timely, with gold and silver prices soaring globally. "Some jewelry customers are turning to new product lines," said Chen Danping, deputy general manager of Guangzhou-based Justop Jewelry. Stainless steel ornaments, Chen explained, combine jewelry-making techniques and appearance with the cost advantage of a much cheaper material. For Jacob Ruiz Palomo, a buyer from Spain, the appeal is straightforward: the jewelry pulls off a commercial trick, making an inexpensive material look anything but cheap. "Its competitive prices need not come at the expense of good design," Palomo noted. This trick points to a broader change in Chinese manufacturing. For decades, China's exporters built their strength on scale, speed and cost. These advantages still matter today, but many manufacturers are aiming higher and trying to win the competition via smarter technologies and better designs. The Canton Fair, China's vast twice-yearly trading floor, offers a snapshot of this transition. Serving as a barometer and wind vane of China's foreign trade, this year's fair, marking its 70th anniversary, has brought together products that seek to compete not only on function and price, but also on intelligence, appearance and design. The fair's 2026 design innovation award, known as the CF Award, offers a glimpse of where Chinese manufacturing design is heading. This year, 222 products from 174 companies made the cut, with AI-powered products accounting for 32 percent of entries and green, low-carbon products for 44 percent. The top award winners included the ZXMOTO 820RR motorcycle and an intelligent capsule robot for gastric endoscopy. Yet the value of design is not confined to high-end products. It can also transform the most ordinary household items, making them more functional and distinctive. At the stand of Guangdong-based brand EKO, a range of stainless-steel rubbish bins showed how thoughtful design can elevate an everyday household item. One model, equipped with an automatic sensor, caught the attention of many buyers. "The company pays attention to details as small as the angle of a corner and the curve of a lid," said Pan Libin, a representative. "Thoughtful design can expand a product's uses," Pan added. "A rubbish bin can fit into different settings, from living rooms and kitchens to bathrooms and bedrooms. We can tailor designs to different needs in terms of size, shape, color and available space." EKO began as an original-equipment manufacturer, making products for other companies. In 2007, it started developing its own brand, betting that design could give it a more distinctive place in the market. One of its products became a Red Dot winner this year, adding international recognition to its effort. For other Chinese companies, drawing on domestic cultural heritage is another way to differentiate a product. Zhu Bingren copper art, based in Hangzhou in east China's Zhejiang Province, is a business featuring craftsmanship spanning multiple generations, and has drawn strong interest from overseas buyers at this year's fair. The business incorporates copper carving techniques, recognized as part of China's national intangible cultural heritage, into products ranging from home ornaments to tea sets, thus transforming centuries-old craftsmanship into contemporary designs for global consumers. "Foreign customers are showing particular interest in traditional Chinese elements," said Gu Dawei, the company's sales manager. "While staying true to our cultural roots, we also pay close attention to the needs and preferences of different markets so that our products can better appeal to consumers around the world." More than 700 samples brought to the fair have been snapped up by buyers, according to the company. Industry insiders said the increased presence of Chinese design in consumer products worldwide is underpinned by the strengths of China's manufacturing ecosystem. Its comprehensive industrial chains allow creative ideas to be turned into tangible products quickly, while efficient supply chains enable manufacturers to respond swiftly to changing market demands. Michael Schjerbeck Jensen, general manager of F&H Asia, told Xinhua that the Danish group's joint product development with Chinese partners has repeatedly turned ideas into reality. In an uncertain world, Jensen said, China's comprehensive, stable and efficient supply chains offer a particularly valuable source of certainty. "The growing international reach of Chinese design is increasingly evident," said Luo Weiyu, business director of 3&1 Industrial Design. "Backed by China's complete industrial chains, domestic designers can also update their concepts and bring new products to market quickly, making them more responsive to consumer demand. More buyers from countries including Italy and Japan are now seeking partnerships with Chinese designers." ■

item.title: China issues 800 bln yuan via financial instruments to expand investment
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
BEIJING, Oct. 28 (Xinhua) -- China has completed the issuance of 800 billion yuan (about 119 billion U.S. dollars) under its 2026 new policy-based financial instruments as of Wednesday, channeling funds to key projects to expand effective investment, according to three policy banks. The China Development Bank allocated 365 billion yuan, involving projects with a total investment of 5.5 trillion yuan, and the Export-Import Bank of China allocated 120 billion yuan, helping leverage over 1.7 trillion yuan in investment, while the Agricultural Development Bank of China allocated 315 billion yuan, featuring projects with a total investment of around 4.39 trillion yuan. First launched in 2025 with an allocation of 500 billion yuan, these instruments prioritize the digital economy, artificial intelligence (AI), consumer infrastructure, and urban renewal endeavors such as transport, energy and underground pipe network upgrades. This year's government work report set the 2026 allocation at 800 billion yuan to attract more private capital. A large share of the funds went to AI and the digital economy. The China Development Bank allocated 179.01 billion yuan to projects in AI, the digital economy, green and low-carbon development, biomedicine and consumption. The Export-Import Bank of China supported more than 220 projects in emerging sectors like the digital economy and AI, with loans to these fields accounting for nearly half of its total allocation. The Agricultural Development Bank of China, meanwhile, supported almost 2,000 projects in areas including AI, the digital economy, the low-altitude economy, consumption and green and low-carbon development, with financing of nearly 200 billion yuan. Support for private investment was also strengthened. The China Development Bank allocated 127.99 billion yuan to projects involving private investment or private capital. The Export-Import Bank of China supported more than 210 such projects, accounting for almost 40 percent of its total allocation, while the Agricultural Development Bank of China supported nearly 400 projects with over 65 billion yuan. All of the 800 billion yuan was used to supplement project capital, helping ease capital shortages for major projects, improve their financing capacity, and leverage bank lending and private capital. Going forward, the three policy banks will strengthen post-investment management, provide supportive loans, and accelerate the conversion of funds into physical work to maximize the instruments' effectiveness. Wen Bin, chief economist at China Minsheng Bank, said the rollout of 800 billion yuan via new policy-based financial instruments, together with major infrastructure projects and urban renewal initiatives, could stimulate demand for electronic information products, electrical machinery, high-end equipment and certain raw materials. ■

item.title: Column: Understanding the strengths of China's governance model
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-28
by Denis Simon As China continues on its development path, a range of complex issues will require sustained attention. The good news is that the track record of the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese government demonstrates a number of institutional strengths and development achievements for dealing with these challenges. To better grasp the capacity of the Chinese government and the CPC to handle the challenges it is confronting, I would like to emphasize three main themes: long-term strategic planning, governance capacity and policy implementation, and the relationship between economic development and improvements in people's livelihoods. STRENGTH OF CHINA'S GOVERNANCE MODEL I believe one of the most important strengths of China's governance model is its ability to combine long-term strategic vision with the capacity to mobilize resources and implement policies on a national scale. One challenge facing many governments today, particularly in developing countries, is the difficulty of maintaining policy continuity. Electoral cycles, political polarization, competing institutional interests, and short-term political calculations can make it difficult to sustain development strategies over a decade or longer. China has developed an institutional approach that places considerable emphasis on long-term planning, policy coordination, and continuity of national development objectives. The five-year planning system is an important illustration. It allows the government to establish priorities, coordinate national and local development strategies, mobilize public and private resources, and adjust policies as circumstances change. China's experience in infrastructure development, poverty reduction, industrial upgrading, and technological advancement demonstrates the potential benefits of this approach. I would identify five lessons that may be relevant to political leaders in developing countries: First, the importance of long-term strategic planning. Governments need to look beyond immediate political and economic pressures and develop a coherent national development vision. Second, the importance of state capacity. Having good policies is not enough. Governments must possess the administrative institutions, professional personnel, financial resources, and organizational capabilities to translate policy objectives into tangible results. China's experience demonstrates the importance of connecting central strategic direction with implementation at provincial, municipal, and grassroots levels. Third, the ability to mobilize resources around national priorities. Developing countries often face severe resource constraints. China's experience illustrates how governments can coordinate public investment, private-sector participation, financial institutions, and local development initiatives to advance major national objectives. Fourth, the importance of pragmatism and policy experimentation. One particularly interesting aspect of China's reform experience has been its willingness to experiment with policies at the local level, evaluate results, and expand successful approaches. The establishment of special economic zones is a prominent example. This suggests that effective governance does not require every policy to be perfect from the beginning. It requires institutional learning and the willingness to correct mistakes. Fifth, the importance of maintaining social stability while pursuing economic transformation. Development requires a reasonably predictable political, social, and economic environment. Governments must address inequality, unemployment, regional disparities, and public concerns if they hope to sustain public confidence. However, China's governance model should not be regarded as a universal template that other country can simply copy. Every country has its own political institutions, historical circumstances, social structures, and development challenges. Different countries may draw useful insights from one another's development experiences. Therefore, the most productive international discussion should focus less on competing political labels and more on identifying practical approaches that improve government effectiveness, strengthen accountability, deliver public services, and create opportunities for economic development. CORE REASON CPC MAINTAINS LONG-TERM GOVERNING VITALITY In my view, the fundamental reason is the ability of the Communist Party of China (CPC) to maintain a strong organizational structure while continuously adapting its governing priorities to China's changing economic and social circumstances. The CPC's longevity cannot be explained simply by its size or organizational reach. Its membership of more than 100 million gives it an extraordinary organizational presence, but size alone does not guarantee governing effectiveness. What matters is how that organization functions and whether it can continue to deliver results. I would highlight three interconnected factors. First, the CPC has developed a distinctive capacity for long-term strategic thinking. It has consistently emphasized national development objectives that extend beyond immediate economic or political considerations. The ability to maintain continuity in major national priorities, while adjusting implementation to changing circumstances, is an important institutional advantage. Second, the Party has demonstrated a considerable capacity for adaptation. Since the beginning of reform and opening-up, China has undergone enormous transformations in its economic structure, social composition, technological capabilities, and international position. The CPC has chosen to adjust its governing approaches to accommodate these changes. The transformation from a predominantly agricultural economy into a major industrial and technological power required not only economic reform but also significant changes in governance, administration and policymaking. Third, the Party has placed considerable emphasis on organizational discipline, cadre development, and the ability to translate central policy decisions into action throughout the country. This capacity for coordination and implementation is an important source of institutional strength. I would add one further consideration: the ultimate test of a ruling party's vitality is whether it retains the capacity to recognize problems, correct mistakes, respond to changing public expectations, and maintain public confidence. No political organization can remain effective simply by relying on its historical achievements. China's economic and social circumstances today are very different from those of 20 or even 10 years ago. The expectations of younger generations, the challenges of an aging population, the pressures of economic restructuring, and the demands of technological innovation all require new governing capabilities. CPC'S PEOPLE-CENTERED PHILOSOPHY OF DEVELOPMENT I consider the people-centered philosophy of development one of the most important aspects of the CPC's governing approach, particularly because it connects national development objectives with the everyday concerns of ordinary citizens. One of the most significant achievements of China's reform and development experience has been the transformation of living conditions for an enormous proportion of its population. Consider poverty alleviation. China's achievement in lifting hundreds of millions of people out of extreme poverty is historically significant. It demonstrates what can be accomplished when poverty reduction becomes a sustained national priority, supported by targeted policies, substantial resource mobilization, infrastructure investment, and local implementation. But the importance of a people-centered philosophy of development should not be measured exclusively by poverty reduction. It also should be reflected in the quality and accessibility of public services, including education, healthcare, employment opportunities, affordable housing, pensions, and social protection. China has made substantial progress in expanding educational opportunities, improving rural infrastructure, extending healthcare coverage, and developing social security systems. These achievements have helped create a much stronger foundation for social and economic development. I also would emphasize an important conceptual point: economic growth and improvements in people's livelihoods should not be treated as separate objectives. They are mutually reinforcing. Economic development creates the resources necessary to improve public services, while better education, healthcare, social protection, and employment opportunities strengthen human capital and support further economic growth. That said, China's people-centered philosophy of development faces an important new test as China has moved into a substantially different stage of development. The challenges today are no longer simply about lifting people out of poverty or expanding basic infrastructure. They increasingly involve improving the quality of development and ensuring that its benefits are shared more equitably. My overall assessment is that China's experience demonstrates the importance of placing improvements in people's living standards at the center of national development. But the next stage will require moving beyond the achievements of poverty reduction and basic development toward greater equality of opportunity, higher-quality public services, and more balanced and sustainable growth. EXPECTATIONS FOR FIFTH PLENARY SESSION I believe the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee comes at an important moment for China. The country is entering a new phase of development, facing a more complicated international environment and a number of significant domestic economic and social challenges. The principal focus of the Fifth Plenary Session is on advancing the Party's full and rigorous self-governance. Against this background, I expect the Fifth Plenary Session to deliver an important message: institutional self-renewal is essential to long-term governing capacity. The CPC has repeatedly emphasized the importance of discipline, combating corruption, and strengthening Party self-governance. I believe this is particularly important at a time when China is confronting more complex economic, technological, and international challenges. But institutional self-renewal must go beyond disciplinary measures. It should also involve improving the quality of governance, strengthening administrative accountability, encouraging innovation, and ensuring that officials at all levels have both the competence and the incentives to address difficult problems. An effective governing party must be capable of renewing itself before institutional weaknesses become serious obstacles to development. Looking ahead, I believe the Fifth Plenary Session could strengthen the CPC's institutional capacity and reinforce the importance of administrative discipline and organizational accountability. It could also send an important signal to the international community about China's approach to governance, economic development, and its role in an increasingly uncertain global environment. Ultimately, my expectation is that the meeting will demonstrate that China's next stage of modernization requires not only strong political leadership and long-term strategic planning, but also continuous institutional reform, greater policy responsiveness, and a stronger commitment to improving people's livelihoods. The most important outcome should not simply be another set of policy declarations. It should be a clearer demonstration of how the CPC intends to translate its governing principles into practical results for the benefit of the entire population. Editor's note: Denis Simon is the former Executive Vice Chancellor of Duke Kunshan University in Jiangsu province. He is also a senior faculty member in the Schwarzman College at Tsinghua University. The views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the positions of Xinhua News Agency. ■

item.title: Why the CPC puts people's well-being at the heart of self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- In northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, eligible residents can receive certain forms of medical assistance and other support without submitting an application. Government departments share the information needed to provide the benefits. The provincial bodies responsible for disciplinary inspection helped drive the change. They prompted civil affairs departments to build a data-sharing network connecting 33 departments and institutions, enabling 12 frequently used assistance services to be provided without applications. The initiative offers a concrete example of how the self-supervision of the Communist Party of China (CPC) improve public services and help ensure that benefits reach those who most need them. Earning public trust through tangible improvements in people's lives is a defining feature of the CPC's full and rigorous self-governance, which is high on the agenda of the fifth plenary session of its 20th Central Committee. The key meeting, which opened Monday in Beijing, is considering a draft decision of the CPC Central Committee on major issues concerning strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance. COMMITMENT TO THE PEOPLE The CPC constitution commits the Party to serving the people, and states that it has no special interests of its own apart from those of the working class and the broadest possible majority of the people. Without seeking self-interest, the CPC can keep its spirit of thorough self-reform, and by swiftly detecting and resolving its own problems, the Party can prevent any interest group, power group or privileged stratum from preying on or corrupting its members. Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, has led an unprecedented anti-corruption campaign since 2012, driven by a determination to "offend a few thousand rather than fail 1.4 billion." The campaign has targeted corrupt officials at both high and low levels. Gyula Thurmer, president of the Hungarian Workers' Party, said serving the interests of the people is a central principle of the CPC. He added that the Party's anti-corruption efforts have achieved significant results, strengthening internal discipline and helping implement major economic and social development programs. SAFEGUARDING PEOPLE'S INTERESTS Xi has called on Party members to bear in mind that "benefiting the people is their greatest political achievement." An official review of work in 2025 reported that disciplinary and supervisory bodies nationwide investigated 967,000 cases of misconduct and corruption affecting people's daily lives, returning or helping recover about 77.6 billion yuan (11.5 billion U.S. dollars) in money and property to the public. Faruk Boric, president of the Association of Friendship between China and Bosnia and Herzegovina, said China's efforts to pursue corrupt officials at both senior and lower levels send "a clear message that no official is above the rules, regardless of their position." He said China's experience offers important lessons in linking clean governance with people's well-being. Protecting public funds, he added, helps direct more resources toward health care, education and other public services. BUILDING BETTER GOVERNANCE On several occasions, Xi has called for taking simultaneous, coordinated, and comprehensive steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity or desire to become corrupt. In his article on the Party's self-reform, Xi urged efforts to improve Party conduct, enforce discipline, and fight corruption, while integrating Party self-supervision with public oversight to deeply advance the Party's self-reform. Lyazid Benhami, a member of the Paris Association of French-Chinese Friendship, said rigorous Party self-governance can clarify officials' responsibilities, improve coordination and help sustain development programs. He highlighted China's emphasis on long-term planning, infrastructure, education and research, adding that the country has achieved a profound transformation regarding such priority areas and improved the well-being of its people. Those administrative strengths matter as China implements its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). In January, Xi urged efforts to confine power to an institutional cage in a more well-conceived and effective manner, and press ahead with the anti-corruption fight with a clearer understanding and stronger resolve, thus providing a strong guarantee for achieving the goals and tasks of the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Volker Tschapke, honorary president of Germany's Prussian Society, said the CPC's courage to "turn the blade inward" demonstrated a "moral strength that I truly admire." He stressed that rigorous Party self-governance ultimately serves the fundamental interests of the people. "I have seen with my own eyes what that has achieved: how villages have blossomed through targeted poverty alleviation, how rural areas have found new hope, how high-speed rail connects people and hearts," he said.■

item.title: Xi congratulates Lula on re-election as Brazilian president
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday extended congratulations to Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election as president of Brazil. In his congratulatory message, Xi said that President Lula has made important contributions to advancing China-Brazil relations. Xi said he and Lula have, in recent years, maintained close communication through various means and jointly guided the building of the China-Brazil community with a shared future for a more just world and a more sustainable planet to new progress. The global, strategic and long-term significance of the bilateral relationship has become increasingly prominent, making it a model of solidarity and cooperation among Global South countries, he said. Xi said that he attaches great importance to the development of China-Brazil relations and stands ready to work with President Lula to guide the building of a China-Brazil community with a shared future to new heights, open up broader prospects for all-round strategic coordination between the two countries, and continuously enhance the well-being of the two peoples. Also on Tuesday, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng sent a congratulatory message to Geraldo Alckmin on his re-election as Brazil's vice president. ■
